one_liner: A standing Library of Congress resume database for applicants with certified severe disabilities, used to fill jobs noncompetitively in any series or grade over two years.
fit_summary: This program is open only to applicants who can submit a certification of a severe disability, and nothing on file indicates Daniel has one. If Daniel does qualify, the fit is good: the Library's Congressional Liaison, Social Science Analyst, Public Affairs and Program Analyst roles match Daniel's policy knowledge, people skills and IEM government-client experience.
eligibility: Limited to applicants with a targeted or severe disability, documented by a certificate from a State Vocational Rehabilitation Office, a college disability or career services office, or the VA.
The disability certification must be dated within 3 years of the closing date (Nov 25, 2026) and submitted with the application, or the application will not be considered.
Each vacancy requires qualifications under the OPM qualification standards for its series and grade, meaning progressively responsible experience at the needed level.
Some series require specific degrees or training, and transcripts and certifications must be uploaded at the time of application.
Security clearance is listed as 'Other', so a background investigation will likely be required.
strategy: First confirm eligibility: apply only if you have, or can obtain, a severe-disability certification (for example, through Virginia's DARS vocational rehabilitation office) dated within 3 years. If not, skip this posting and target open Library of Congress or congressional vacancies instead.

Because this is a two-year resume database, tailor the resume toward 2-3 target series (Congressional Liaison, Public Affairs, Program Analyst) so that managers pulling lists can quickly see the match.

Frame the IEM role by its actual duties: government client relationships, stakeholder coordination, policy or program analysis, and preparedness or recovery program support. Include dates, hours per week and concrete scope for each.
The posting allows longer resumes, but keep the main resume concise (two pages is safest under OPM's rule) and put detail in clear duty statements rather than long narratives.
Upload all documents at once: the disability certificate, the resume, and any transcripts. Contact spp@loc.gov or 202-707-6024 with any questions about certification.
Apply early rather than near the November 2026 close, since lists can be pulled at any time.
resume_bullets: Served as [title] at IEM, supporting [federal/state/local agency] clients on [emergency management/disaster recovery program], coordinating with [number/type] of stakeholders ([hours] hrs/week).
Researched and analyzed [policy/regulation/program topic] and produced [briefs/reports] used by [client or leadership] to [decision or action].
Built working relationships with [elected officials/agency staff/public groups] by [method], resulting in [outcome you can verify].
interview_questions: Describe a time you explained a complex policy issue to a non-expert audience.
How have you managed relationships with government clients or stakeholders who had competing priorities?
Tell us about a research or analysis project you led from start to finish.
Why do you want to work at the Library of Congress, and in which service unit?
watch_outs: Disability certification is mandatory; without it, Daniel cannot be considered under this program.
This is a resume database, not a specific job, so there may be no contact for months.
The program confers no promotion eligibility, and the positions are on-site with no telework.
Some target series may require specific degrees, so check the OPM standard for each series before claiming qualification.
